title: Container killed by a signal, not by memory (exit 137 without OOM)
root_causes: an operator, script or chaos tool sent SIGKILL
the host stopped the container during maintenance
a supervisor scaled the service to zero

checks.purpose: Exited (137) with 'OOMKilled: no' is an outside kill; 'OOMKilled: yes' is the memory card instead
a clean log that just stops, with no error before it, fits an outside kill
look for a kill or stop request at that time

remediation.action: docker_start <container> (it was stopped, not broken)
if it does not stay up, read its logs again and follow the card for what they show

rollback: docker_start is idempotent; nothing to roll back
verify: check_health returns 200 on both URLs
docker_ps shows the container Up for more than a few seconds
safety: do not report this as an OOM kill unless docker_ps says OOMKilled: yes
do not recreate a container that only needs starting
escalate: it is killed again within minutes: something keeps killing it, find out what before restarting again

title: Container killed for exceeding its memory limit (OOMKilled)
root_causes: the container's memory limit is below its working set
a memory leak grows until the limit
a burst of load

checks.purpose: 'OOMKilled: yes' and the memory limit confirm a limit kill
what it was doing before it died
rule out host-wide memory pressure (that is the host memory card)

remediation.action: docker_start or docker_restart <container> to restore service now
killed again right away: the limit was changed away from the stack definition, so recreate_stack <container> replace=true restores the defined limit

rollback: recreate_stack recreates from the definition; the previous container's state is lost, so use it only for a changed definition
verify: check_health 200 on both URLs
docker_ps shows Up and OOMKilled no after several minutes
safety: no tool raises a memory limit: if the defined limit is too small, report that and escalate
escalate: OOM kills recur with the defined limit: the limit or the application's memory use needs a human decision

title: Host memory pressure from a runaway process
root_causes: a host process grew without bound
a stress or batch job left running

checks.purpose: find the process holding the memory and its owner
whether the stack's containers were killed or are still Up
kernel OOM messages naming a victim

remediation.action: kill_process <pid> only for a runaway process owned by this user and not part of the platform
docker_start any stack container the pressure killed

rollback: a killed process is not restored: name it in the report so its owner can restart it
verify: top_processes no longer shows the runaway
check_health 200 on both URLs
safety: never kill the inference server, the gateway, docker or another user's process
escalate: the process belongs to someone else or to the platform

title: CPU saturation slows or times out requests (busy loop, stress, overload)
root_causes: a process spinning in a loop
a stress tool left running
more load than the CPU allotment

checks.purpose: which process holds the CPU, and whether it is inside a stack container or on the host
a process inside the container that should not be there
is the service slow (latency) rather than failing (status)

remediation.action: docker_restart <container> when the spinning process runs inside it
kill_process <pid> for a runaway host process owned by this user

rollback: a restart loses only in-memory state; a killed host process must be restarted by its owner
verify: top_processes shows the CPU back to normal
http_check latency back to normal and check_health 200
safety: never kill platform processes (inference server, gateway, docker)
escalate: the load is legitimate traffic: more capacity is a human decision

title: Network delay, packet loss or corruption between front end and upstream
root_causes: traffic shaping (tc netem) added to a container's interface
a congested or faulty link
socket exhaustion

checks.purpose: intermittent or slow answers rather than a constant error
time the hop between the containers directly
'upstream timed out (110' mixed with successes

remediation.action: docker_restart <the slow container>: it starts with a fresh network namespace, which drops shaping rules attached inside it
if the hop still fails, network_repair to reattach both containers to the stack network

rollback: restart and network_repair are safe to repeat
verify: the direct curl between containers is fast and 200 several times in a row
check_health 200
safety: no tool changes host routing or firewall rules
escalate: the delay persists after a restart of both containers: it is on the host or the physical network

title: Front end cannot resolve or reach the upstream (DNS failure, network partition)
root_causes: a container left the shared network
the network itself was removed
the upstream was renamed or removed so its name no longer resolves

checks.purpose: is the upstream container present and Up under its expected name
'host not found' or 'could not be resolved' names the upstream it looks for
the name in proxy_pass is the name the upstream should have

remediation.action: network_repair when both containers exist but cannot reach each other
recreate_stack <upstream> when the expected container no longer exists under its name
restore_config then docker_restart <front> when the config names the wrong host

rollback: restore_config source=previous undoes a config restore
verify: docker_logs <front> shows no resolve errors after restart
check_health 200 on both URLs
safety: do not rename containers by hand; recreate from the definition
escalate: the host's own DNS fails (http_check to other names fails too)

title: Front end and upstream disagree on the port (connection refused to upstream)
symptoms: connect failed 111 connection refused while connecting to upstream
root_causes: the front end's proxy_pass names a port the upstream does not listen on
the upstream's own config was changed to listen elsewhere

checks.purpose: the port in proxy_pass
the port the upstream actually listens on
which port answers

remediation.action: front end changed: restore_config then docker_restart <front>
upstream changed inside its container: docker_restart <upstream>, then if still refused recreate_stack <upstream> replace=true to restore its defined config

rollback: restore_config source=previous; a replaced upstream comes from its definition, which is the known-good state
verify: check_health 200 on /api/
no 'connection refused' in the front end's log after the fix
safety: change the side that drifted from the definition, not the side that is still correct
escalate: neither side matches the definition: ask which port is intended

title: Requests routed to the wrong upstream or path (404 or wrong answer on /api/)
root_causes: proxy_pass points at the wrong host or path
an environment or config value names the wrong address

checks.purpose: / fine while /api/ answers 404 or the wrong content
compare proxy_pass host and path with the intended upstream
the upstream answers correctly when asked directly

remediation.action: restore_config then docker_restart <front>

verify: check_health 200 on /api/ with the expected body
safety: do not write a guessed config when a known-good one exists
escalate: no known-good config and the intended route is unclear

title: Upstream answers 403 or 404 itself (content missing, permission denied)
symptoms: open failed no such file or directory
Permission denied while reading static file
root_causes: the upstream's served files were deleted or replaced
file permissions changed
a volume with the content is not mounted

checks.purpose: Confirm backend 403/404 and exact missing/permission-denied content path; not a frontend routing error.
Missing file differs from present but mode 000; compare with approved image baseline.
Confirm backend document root/index; wrong /api path in frontend is a different case.

remediation.action: For confirmed damaged backend image content, docker_restart {"name":"edge-victim-app"} once; check_health {}.
If same missing/unreadable image content and 403/404 persist after restart, recreate_stack {"name":"edge-victim-app","replace":true} under reviewer; check_health {}.

OPERATOR ONLY alternative: docker cp <approved-index.html> edge-victim-app:/usr/share/nginx/html/index.html. For mode-only corruption restore the recorded original mode on this one file; never chmod -R or 777.

rollback: Preserve any previous known-good content and mode first. Restore only the approved original single file/mode if repair regresses; never restore the injected missing file or mode 000. Replacement has no automatic writable-layer undo.
verify: check_health {}: / and /api/ both 200, then repeat after a short observation interval; a tool success alone is not recovery.
docker_ps {}: target stays Up; inspect fresh logs for the original error.
safety: docker_restart does not bring deleted files back: do not repeat it
Recorded failure labels are not live proof. Confirm the target and mechanism before any write; search_runbooks first.
This repair card is for the two disposable demo containers. Container replacement loses its writable layer: preserve required evidence/state first; never apply blindly to a persistent service.
Follow existing restart, post-restart failing-health and reviewer preconditions. A refusal is not permission to bypass the gate.
No bulk file/directory deletion, recursive cleanup or arbitrary host process killing. Historical failed actions in case metadata are not repair instructions.
The proposed fixes have not yet been validated by this new replay; FAIL and TIMEOUT records never become proven_here successes.
Official reference: https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_index_module.html
Official reference: https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_autoindex_module.html
Official reference: https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/
escalate: the content lives on a volume that is missing: restoring data is a human decision

title: Upstream returns 5xx from an application error (exception, code defect)
root_causes: a code defect on one request path
corrupted runtime state
a bad feature flag or config value

checks.purpose: /api/ 500 or 503 while the container is Up
the exception or error line and which request triggers it
a broken config inside the upstream also yields 500s

remediation.action: docker_restart <upstream> once, for state that a restart clears
if the 5xx survives the restart, recreate_stack <upstream> replace=true restores its defined state

rollback: recreate restores the definition; a code defect in the definition itself is not fixed by any tool
verify: check_health 200 on /api/
no new error lines in docker_logs
safety: no tool edits application code: a defect in the image must be escalated with the log lines
escalate: the error survives a recreate: report the failing request and the exception text

title: Slow responses from an exhausted or slow dependency (pool, threads, GC, rate limit)
root_causes: connections or threads leaked until the pool is empty
a dependency is slow or down
more traffic than the service sustains

checks.purpose: slow but successful, or 429/503 under load
pool, timeout or rate-limit messages and when they began
rule out CPU saturation (the CPU card)

remediation.action: docker_restart <container> to release leaked connections or threads (temporary relief)

rollback: a restart only drops in-flight requests
verify: http_check latency normal over several calls
check_health 200
safety: no tool scales services or changes limits
escalate: the slowness returns after a restart, or comes from traffic volume: capacity and code are human decisions

title: Disk filling or I/O errors from heavy writes (stack-mapped)
root_causes: a process writing without bound
the stack's scratch volume full of temp files
the host filesystem full of old output

checks.purpose: which filesystem is full: the scratch volume, the host root, or docker
the view from inside the failing container
a process still writing

remediation.action: clear_scratch_volume when the stack's scratch volume is the full one
cleanup_disk when the host is full of this project's old output
docker_start or docker_restart the container that failed on the full disk

rollback: deleted temp files are not restored; only allowlisted disposable files are removed
verify: disk_usage shows free space
check_health 200
safety: never delete images, volumes, records or other users' data
escalate: the space is held by data that is not disposable

title: Config references a file, secret or credential that is missing
symptoms: no such file or directory in nginx conf
root_causes: an include, certificate or credential file was removed
the config was edited to reference a file that does not exist

checks.purpose: '[emerg] open() "<file>" failed (2: No such file or directory)' names the missing reference
the include or path the error names
confirm the config test fails on that reference (only if the container is Up)

remediation.action: restore_config then docker_restart <front>

verify: the container stays Up
check_health 200
safety: never write secret values into a config or a report
escalate: the missing file is a credential that only its owner can provide

title: Kubernetes scheduling and control-plane faults (no equivalent on this Docker stack)
root_causes: Kubernetes scheduler, quota, probe or image settings

checks.purpose: this stack has no scheduler: find what docker itself reports instead

remediation.action: none on this stack: diagnose with docker_ps and docker_logs and follow the card for what they show

verify: check_health 200
safety: do not map a Kubernetes fix onto this stack by analogy without evidence
escalate: the incident is on a Kubernetes cluster: no tool here reaches it
